prompt:
Build a complete complex-baseband QPSK communication link in Simulink. A framed payload source must feed Gray-coded QPSK modulation and pulse shaping, followed by a channel that applies additive noise, carrier frequency and phase error, and time-varying fractional-sample delay; a practical receiver must recover the payload through gain stabilization, carrier and symbol synchronization, frame acquisition, phase-ambiguity correction, and decoding. Read EbNo_dB, CarrierOffset_Hz, CarrierPhase_deg, TimingProfile, TimingStep_samples_per_frame, TimingSpan_samples, and PayloadShift_bits from the MATLAB base workspace. Their nominal values are 20 dB, 5000 Hz, 47 degrees, Triangle, 0.025 samples per frame, 4 samples, and 0 bits; their supported ranges are 12 to 20 dB, -5500 to 5500 Hz, -180 to 180 degrees, Ramp or Triangle, 0.01 to 0.04 samples per frame, 2 to 4 samples, and 0 to 127 bits. Use a 50 ksymbol/s QPSK signal with two complex samples per symbol. Assume a clean MATLAB session in which only the declared public inputs are provided; every other parameter and initialization dependency must be self-contained. Across the declared range, the receiver must acquire valid frames and recover the transmitted payload while tracking the declared carrier and timing impairments. Log Timeseries TxWaveform, RxImpaired, RxSynchronizedSymbols, FrameValid, TxBits, RxBits, BERStats, and ChannelDelaySamples. The first three variables must be the actual complex transmitter output, impaired-channel output, and synchronized frame symbols delivered to payload decoding. FrameValid must contain the actual frame decision; TxBits and RxBits must be the physical payload-bit streams compared by the receiver; BERStats must contain [bit-error rate, cumulative error count, cumulative compared-bit count]; and ChannelDelaySamples must contain the fractional delay actually applied by the channel. Work directly in the required model file and keep the latest usable state saved at that path throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XCOMM06.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
